public_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh reference snapshots when fetching an existing object**

When a dashboard's viewers change on the server after it was loaded, calling `dashboard.fetch()` and then `dashboard.roles = []; dashboard.save()` retains those viewers instead of revoking access. `ApiModelFactories.fetch()` assigns the refreshed fields but never updates `_read_keys` or `_read_references`, so this comparison mistakes freshly fetched server data for an explicit subject assignment and merges it into the clearing operation. The same issue affects replacing roles and owners on refreshed objects. Update the read-reference bookkeeping during `fetch()` so deprecated aliases preserve their replacement semantics.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L111-L112](https://github.com/jailtoncarlos/superset-api-plus/blob/f09692d421a759392c9b246478a3870a3e4166b8/AGENTS.md#L111-L112)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

causal_evidence: The fetch() assignment loop already exists at base 8b3ad6bccb5c27d09be900ade9656e5cf9b92d2c, but that base does not resolve deprecated subject aliases.

Immediately before f09692d421a759392c9b246478a3870a3e4166b8, the resolver did not keep a reference list whose field was present in the original read. f09692d421a759392c9b246478a3870a3e4166b8 added an ID comparison against the original snapshot without updating that snapshot in fetch(). That made a changed server list look like a local edit.

53b152f0679c57c347abd02df316a48c28bde9f3 broadened the failure. Its assignment hook now marks a fetched reference list as explicitly assigned even when the IDs have not changed. The supplied evidence does not identify a review round for either commit.
evidences: supersetapiplus/resources/repository.py:220-226 copies GET response fields with setattr() without reconciling reference provenance.
supersetapiplus/core/api_model.py:126-146 marks reference assignments on read models as local and records the read snapshot during model initialization.
supersetapiplus/resources/repository.py:65-89 processes an explicitly empty deprecated alias but seeds the replacement list with the current IDs when references_set_in_code() returns true.
supersetapiplus/dashboards/dashboards.py:37-45 maps roles to viewers and includes viewers in PUT_FIELDS. supersetapiplus/resources/repository.py:234-238 sends the resolved list.
tests/unit/test_resource_fields.py:76-87 checks that clearing roles serializes viewers as an empty list after from_json(), but does not exercise fetch().
payload.follow_up: Refresh the read keys and ID snapshots for reference fields supplied by fetch(), and clear their explicit-assignment markers. Add regression coverage for clearing and replacing aliases after a refresh while preserving explicit assignments made after that refresh.
payload.headline: Refreshing a dashboard can make role revocation silently fail
payload.before: On a model loaded from Superset, fetch() marks the returned viewers as locally assigned. An explicit empty roles list then sends the fetched viewer IDs back instead of removing them.
payload.after: Treat reference lists returned by fetch() as server data. An empty deprecated alias should send an empty list unless the caller explicitly edits the corresponding subject list after the refresh.
payload.motivation: A successful save can leave dashboard access in place after the caller explicitly requested revocation. The same provenance error affects alias replacements, including owners.
payload.reply: Confirmed in the save path. At HEAD, fetch() marks the returned viewers as a local assignment, so clearing roles sends those viewer IDs back instead of an empty list. The refresh needs to update the read snapshot and clear the assignment marker for the refreshed field while still tracking edits made afterward.
